- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Underestimates sharp upward moves (spikes) in true outcomes, particularly after a recent low or recovery phase.
- Overestimates downward moves, especially when history shows recent volatility or mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends.
- Overreacts to recent high prices, producing exaggerated peaks that don’t materialize in true outcomes.
- Underreacts to recent low prices, failing to anticipate rebounds or mean reversion.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting calibration issue with volatility or trend persistence.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, model should reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid overconfidence.
- When true outcome is below forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, model should increase forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid underestimation.
- Avoid using recent high as anchor for next period’s forecast — instead, use 3–5 day moving average or smoothed trend.
- For spikes, model should not forecast 2–3 days ahead unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of upward momentum.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion, model should reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.
- Model underestimates long-term trend (30d) when true outcome shows strong upward momentum — should adjust upward by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days.
- Model overestimates short-term volatility — should reduce forecast variance by 10–20% for 30d horizon.
